newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES A NOTCH UP DESPITE LIQUIDITY.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES A NOTCH UP DESPITE LIQUIDITY.

text.p: Short-term interest rates on Zimbabwe's money market were quoted a touch firmer despite liquidity in the system on Wednesday, dealers said.

The market opened Z$27 million short but the central Reserve Bank forecast a surplus at the end of the day from maturities and auctioned Z$400 million worth of 91-day treasury bills at a steady average rate of 24.88 percent.
Treasury bills were also trading in the secondary market at market at 24.80 percent from 24.75 percent while call money added one percentage point to 23 percent.
NCDs with maturity of 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought at 26.25 percent, slightly up from 26 and sold at 26 percent from 25.5 percent.
Bankers acceptances were also quoted firmer at 25.5 percent from 25 (buying) and were selling at 25 percent from 24.75.
